info.title: EntryBit API
info.summary: Sign in with EntryBit (OAuth2/OIDC) + guest-pass API for apps, servers and SDKs.
info.description:
The public EntryBit API.

## Three ways to authenticate

1. **OAuth2 / OpenID Connect (user-delegated)** — for apps acting on behalf of a signed-in EntryBit user (e.g. the resident mobile app). Authorization-code flow with **PKCE (S256) required**; tokens from `POST /api/oauth/token`. Endpoints under `/api/v1/*` accept the resulting Bearer access token (RS256 JWT, ~15 min) and are additionally bound by the user's organization role.
2. **Organization API keys (server-to-server)** — for backends and SDKs acting as the organization. Keys look like `eb_sk_…`, are created by an org admin in **Settings → API keys**, are shown exactly once, and carry least-privilege scopes. Send as `Authorization: Bearer eb_sk_…` (or `X-API-Key`). Endpoints under `/api/v1/org/*`.
3. **Discovery** — everything self-describes at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`; token signatures verify against `/.well-known/jwks.json`.

## Conventions

- **Errors**: protocol endpoints return RFC 6749/6750 error objects (`{"error": …}` with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge on 401/403). Business endpoints return `{"success": false, "error": …}` or `{"code", "message"}`; quota exhaustion is **402** with `dimension`/`limit`/`current` fields.
- **Rate limits**: per-IP and per-credential buckets; exceeding one returns **429** — back off and retry.
- **Security**: never place credentials in URLs; all endpoints require TLS; `Cache-Control: no-store` on every credential-bearing response. Refresh tokens rotate on every use — always persist the newest one.

get.description: Every endpoint, scope and capability of the authorization server. OIDC libraries configure themselves from this single URL.
RS256 public keys for verifying access tokens and id_tokens offline.

Open in the user's browser (native apps: the SYSTEM browser per RFC 8252 — never a WebView). EntryBit runs login (password, passkey, Google, 2FA) and consent, then 302-redirects to your registered `redirect_uri` with `code`, `state` and `iss` (RFC 9207). **PKCE S256 is mandatory.** Protocol errors after client validation are returned to the redirect_uri as `error`/`error_description`; an invalid `client_id`/`redirect_uri` pair gets a direct 400 (never a redirect).

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Byte-exact match against the client's registered list.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space-delimited subset of the client's allowed scopes. Default: `openid profile email`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque CSRF value, echoed back verbatim. Strongly recommended.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: Binds the id_token to this request. Required if you validate id_tokens client-side.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: Space-set of `none`, `login`, `consent`. `login` forces a fresh sign-in; `none` fails fast (`login_required`/`consent_required`) instead of showing UI.

parameters.name: max_age
parameters.description: Maximum seconds since the user last authenticated; older sessions re-authenticate.

302.description: Redirect: to your `redirect_uri` with `code`+`state`+`iss` on success (or `error` params), or to the EntryBit login/consent UI mid-flow.

400.description: Invalid client_id or redirect_uri (rendered directly — never redirected).

post.summary: Exchange a code, or refresh tokens
post.description: Machine endpoint (CORS-open, no cookies). Public clients authenticate with PKCE; confidential clients add HTTP Basic or `client_secret_post`. **Refresh tokens rotate**: every refresh returns a NEW `refresh_token` — persist it; replaying an old one revokes the whole token family.

400.description: Protocol error (`invalid_grant`, `invalid_request`, `invalid_scope`, `unsupported_grant_type`). Descriptions are deliberately generic.

post.summary: Introspect a token (RFC 7662, confidential clients only)
post.description: Resource-server lookup, bound to the calling client — a client can only introspect tokens issued to it. Anything invalid reads as the flat `{"active": false}`.
Revokes the token and its whole rotation family when it belongs to the calling client. Always returns 200 — even for unknown tokens (no token scanning).

200.description: Revoked (or token was unknown — indistinguishable by design).

get.description: Requires the `openid` scope; `email`/`profile` scopes gate the corresponding claims.

Open in the browser to end the user's EntryBit web session. The session is terminated ONLY when `id_token_hint` verifies and matches the signed-in user (forced-logout-CSRF defense); the browser is then redirected to `post_logout_redirect_uri` ONLY if it exactly matches the client's registered post-logout list — otherwise to the EntryBit home page.

parameters.name: id_token_hint
parameters.description: The id_token previously issued to the client (may be expired; signature must verify).

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Optional; must match the hint's audience when present.

302.description: Redirect to the registered post-logout URI (with `state`) or the EntryBit home page.

post.description: Same contract as GET with the parameters in an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body.

get.description: Keyset-paginated list of passes the user created, newest first. The first page carries the monthly invite-allowance `usage` block. Requires the user to still hold the organization's self-invite role.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match on guest name / email / phone.

post.description: Creates 1–10 passes with distinct QR credentials, scoped to a facility's doors, and delivers ONE email/SMS carrying a single pass link. Counts against the user's monthly invite allowance (all-or-nothing for the batch).

get.summary: Get one of the user's passes

delete.summary: Revoke one of the user's active passes
delete.description: Cancels the pass AND deactivates its QR credential on the door hardware. Only passes the user created, and only while still active (`expected`/`registered`).

409.description: The pass is no longer active.

get.description: The facility ids needed for POST /api/v1/passes. Same scope + tenant gate as pass creation.

get.summary: List ALL passes in the organization
get.description: Company-wide, keyset-paginated. Rows include `created_by` (the inviting user's id) for attribution.

post.summary: Create guest pass(es) as the organization
post.description: Same body and behavior as the user-delegated create; attribution and invite quota go to the admin who minted the key. Requires the `org:passes:write` scope.

delete.summary: Revoke ANY active pass in the organization
delete.description: Cancels the pass and deactivates its QR credential — regardless of which user created it (still tenant-scoped to the key's organization).

409.description: The pass is no longer active.

get.description: The facility ids an SDK needs to create passes.

Keyset-paginated, ordered by `created_at DESC, id DESC`. Dual-authenticated: an organization API key (`org:members:read` = basic fields; `org:members:contact:read` adds email/phone) OR a delegated OAuth token (`members:read` + the user's live `employees:view` org permission — a delegated token reads exactly what its user sees on the web roster, contact fields included). `fields` selects a comma-separated subset; an unknown field is a 400 listing `allowed_fields`, a field above the key's tier is a 403 `insufficient_scope` naming the missing scope. Deactivated members are excluded unless `status` says otherwise.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches the member's name (plus email/phone on the contact tier).

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated field subset, e.g. `id,name,email`. Default: every field the token's tier allows.

get.summary: Read one member of the organization
get.description: Same auth models, field tiers and `fields` selection as the listing. Inactive members ARE returned (with `status: inactive`) — their id stays addressable, Directory-style.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated field subset. Default: every field the token's tier allows.

EntryBitOAuth.description: Authorization-code flow. PKCE (S256) is REQUIRED for every client; public clients (mobile/SPA) have no secret.

scopes.offline_access: Stay signed in (issue a refresh token)
scopes.passes:write: Create and manage your guest passes
scopes.member:read: Your member profile, organization and apartment details

OAuthAccessToken.description: An EntryBit access token (RS256 JWT, `typ: at+jwt`) from POST /api/oauth/token. Verifiable offline against /.well-known/jwks.json.

OrgApiKey.description: An organization API key (created in Settings → API keys, shown once). 256-bit secret; optional expiry and source-IP allowlist; least-privilege org:* scopes.

OrgApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
OrgApiKeyHeader.description: Alternative header for the organization API key.

InvalidToken.description: Missing, malformed, expired or revoked access token.

InvalidApiKey.description: Missing, unknown, revoked, expired or IP-restricted API key (indistinguishable by design).

InsufficientScope.description: The credential lacks a required scope (the `WWW-Authenticate` challenge names it), or the acting user's organization role was revoked.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests — back off and retry.

NotFound.description: No such resource in the caller's scope.

ValidationError.description: The request body failed validation (the `message`/`error` says which field).

QuotaExceeded.description: The monthly invite allowance can't fit the batch (all-or-nothing).

DiscoveryDocument.description: OIDC Discovery / RFC 8414 metadata (key fields shown; consult the live document).

code.description: The one-time code from the redirect (60 s TTL, single use).

redirect_uri.description: Must equal the authorize request's redirect_uri byte-for-byte.

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose S256 hash was sent to /authorize.

client_secret.description: Confidential clients only (or use HTTP Basic).

refresh_token.description: The CURRENT refresh token (they rotate on every use).

client_secret.description: Confidential clients only (or use HTTP Basic).

scope.description: Optional NARROWING of the granted scope (never widening).

access_token.description: RS256 JWT (`typ: at+jwt`), ~15 minutes. Send as `Authorization: Bearer …`.

refresh_token.description: Present when `offline_access` was granted. Rotates on every refresh — always persist the newest.

id_token.description: OIDC id_token (present with `openid`): `sub`, identity claims, `nonce`, `auth_time`, `amr` (how the user authenticated — e.g. ["swk","user"] for a passkey), `at_hash`.

Pass.description: A guest pass. PII fields are decrypted server-side for authorized callers only.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page.

AllowanceUsage.description: Monthly invite allowance (first page only, user-delegated listing).

PassCreateRequest.description: At least one delivery channel (`email` or `phone`) is required so the guest can receive their pass.

phone.description: Delivery channel — the pass SMS. 7–15 digits.

arrival_time.description: `HH:MM`; access starts here (default: start of the arrival day).

access_until.description: Optional pass expiry (default: end of the arrival day). Must not precede arrival_date.

facility_id.description: Which facility's entry doors the QR opens. Must be active.

quantity.description: Create N distinct passes in one call — one email/SMS with a single batch link.

invited_by.description: Display name shown to the guest.

qr_value.description: First pass's QR value (also in the delivered email).

qr_values.description: Every issued QR value, in creation order.

qr_sent.description: Whether the pass email was delivered.

sms_sent.description: Whether the pass SMS was delivered.

pass_link.description: The single shareable pass page URL (shows all QRs in the batch).

phone.description: The member's own account phone number (the one SMS sign-in uses), decrypted server-side. Admin-defined member-field phones arrive via member_fields.values instead.

member_fields.description: Custom member fields the org admin filled in (e.g. apartment number/size). Private admin-only fields are never included.

Member.description: A directory member. Which keys are present depends on the `fields` selection and the token's tier: BASIC = id, name, first_name, last_name, job_title, department, status, created_at; CONTACT (`org:members:contact:read`, or any delegated `members:read` token) adds email and phone.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page.

OAuthError.description: RFC 6749 error object. Descriptions are deliberately generic (no token-state oracle) — branch on `error`, never on the text.

BearerError.description: RFC 6750 challenge body; the `WWW-Authenticate` response header carries the same code (and the missing scope on 403).

AppError.description: Business-error envelope (one of two equivalent shapes).
